record.paper_title: Advances in periodic difference equations with open problems
record.context_brief: Minimal period of merged periodic sequences
record.original_question: Let {a_n} and {b_n} be periodic sequences with least periods q1 and q2. Fix integers k1 and k2, and form a merged sequence by outputting k1 consecutive terms of {a_n}, then k2 consecutive terms of {b_n}, and repeating this process indefinitely. Determine the minimal period of the merged sequence in full generality, without assuming that the two original sequences are disjoint.

evidence.quote: Suppose we have two periodic sequences {an} and {bn} of periods q1 and q2, respectively. ... The obtained signal has the structure [an, bn] := a1, a2, . . . , ak1, b1, b2, . . . , bk2, ak1+1, ak1+2, . . .
Open Problem 4.1. For n ∈ N, let {an} and {bn} be two periodic sequences of periods q1 and q2, respectively. Find the minimal period of the sequence [an, bn] formed in (4.1).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\{a_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ and $\{b_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be two sequences of complex (or real) numbers that are periodic with least periods $q_1$ and $q_2$, respectively; that is, $q_1$ is the smallest positive integer such that $a_{n+q_1}=a_n$ for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$, and similarly for $q_2$. Fix positive integers $k_1$ and $k_2$. Define the merged sequence $[a_n,b_n]$ by concatenating, in order, $k_1$ consecutive terms of $\{a_n\}$ followed by $k_2$ consecutive terms of $\{b_n\}$, and repeating this pattern indefinitely. Explicitly, the merged sequence is
$$a_1,a_2,\dots,a_{k_1},\,b_1,b_2,\dots,b_{k_2},\,a_{k_1+1},a_{k_1+2},\dots,a_{2k_1},\,b_{k_2+1},b_{k_2+2},\dots,b_{2k_2},\,a_{2k_1+1},\dots$$
so that each successive block of $k_1$ terms is drawn (in order, continuing from where the previous $a$-block ended) from $\{a_n\}$, and each successive block of $k_2$ terms is drawn (in order, continuing from where the previous $b$-block ended) from $\{b_n\}$. Determine, in full generality (with no assumption that the ranges of $\{a_n\}$ and $\{b_n\}$ are disjoint), a closed-form expression for the least period of the merged sequence $[a_n,b_n]$ in terms of $q_1$, $q_2$, $k_1$, and $k_2$ (and, when necessary, the values of the sequences themselves).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a survey on periodic difference equations. No web evidence was found indicating that a complete, fully general solution (without the disjointness assumption on the two sequences) has been published.
